headline: People see AI as aware but not conscious

sources.title: AI can act exactly like a human, but we still don't think it's conscious (ScienceDaily)
When AI behaves like us, we still don't think it is conscious (LMU Munich)
AI Can Be Aware, But Humans Draw the Line at Consciousness, New Study Finds (The Debrief)

chunks.text: AI chatbots can talk, answer questions and help with work. To many users, they {{come across as}} almost human. Researchers at the University of Munich in Germany asked if people think these machines are [[conscious]]. They {{looked into}} the question in a study in the [[science journal]] Cognition. The university shared the results on October 2, 2026.

verbs.correct: To seem a certain way to others
verbs.wrong: To copy the voice of a person
verbs.why: He comes across as shy, but he is very funny. A short email often comes across as rude. To many users, AI chatbots come across as almost human.

verbs.wrong: To ask people to join a study
verbs.why: Many researchers look into how people trust new technology. Police look into the cause of every big fire. Researchers in Munich looked into whether people think AI is conscious.

chunks.text: The team {{set up}} several experiments with nearly 1,100 people. Each person read short [[scenarios]] about a [[character]]. Some people read about an AI. Others read the same stories about a human instead. In one example, the character reacted to a sound. In another, it could {{pick up on}} someone's [[emotional state]]. People then [[rated]] how conscious and how [[aware]] each character was of its [[surroundings]].

verbs.wrong: To check the results of a test
verbs.why: Science teachers set up simple experiments for their students. Researchers often set up tests with hundreds of volunteers. The team set up several experiments with nearly 1,100 people.
Dogs often pick up on their owner's mood. Good teachers pick up on a student's worry quickly. In one story, the character could pick up on someone's emotional state.

chunks.text: In both versions, the AI and the human did exactly the same things. Nobody could {{tell them apart}} by their actions. When a human or AI character reacted more to the world around it, its scores {{went up}}. But on consciousness, people showed a [[clear gap]]. Even the most [[responsive]] AI {{fell behind}} the least responsive human. The researchers say people {{hold back}} from calling AI conscious, even when it acts like a human.

verbs.correct: To see the difference between two things
verbs.wrong: To say which of two you like better
verbs.why: The twins look so alike that their teachers rarely tell them apart. Bank workers tell real and fake money apart by touch. The AI and the human acted the same, so nobody could tell them apart by their actions.
The price of eggs goes up every winter. Test scores usually go up after extra practice. When a character reacted more to the world around it, its scores went up.

verbs.correct: To get a lower score than another
verbs.wrong: To be tested by a different group
verbs.why: Students who miss class often fall behind in math. A team that loses its star often falls behind in the second half. Even the most responsive AI fell behind the least responsive human on consciousness.

verbs.correct: To choose not to do something
verbs.wrong: To change your answer at the end
verbs.why: Many people hold back from saying what they really think. Shy workers hold back in meetings because they fear sounding rude. People hold back from calling AI conscious, even when it acts like a human.

chunks.text: The word aware gave a different result. People [[judged]] awareness in much the same way for AI and humans, and the gap mostly {{went away}}. A [[philosopher]] on the team said people may {{end up}} using words about the mind for AI only because they [[lack]] better ones. Another [[senior author]] said companies and journalists often {{talk up}} AI. They describe it as having plans and even a [[conscience]]. He said [[word choice]] matters. The study does not try to {{figure out}} whether AI really is conscious.

verbs.why: A small headache usually goes away after a short rest. The morning fog goes away by noon. With the word aware, the gap between AI and humans mostly went away.

verbs.correct: To finally find yourself doing something
verbs.wrong: To choose your words with great care
verbs.why: Drivers who get lost often end up in the wrong town. People who don't save money often end up in debt. People may end up using words about the mind for AI only because they lack better ones.

verbs.wrong: To build and sell a product
verbs.why: Coaches often talk up new players to reporters. Real estate agents always talk up the houses they sell. A senior author said companies and journalists often talk up AI.

verbs.correct: To find the answer to something
verbs.wrong: To give money for a new study
verbs.why: Most people figure out a new phone in a few days. A good mechanic quickly figures out why a car doesn't start. The study does not try to figure out whether AI really is conscious.

Let's set up a call with the whole team.

ex: It is hard to tell these two birds apart.

ex: We ended up eating at home because it was raining.
She ended up working at the same company as her father.

wordDefs.def: Able to feel and have experiences of your own
ex: Some people believe that animals are conscious.
Scientists still argue about what makes a living thing conscious.
Is a fish conscious in the same way a dog is?

wordDefs.def: A magazine that prints new research by scientists
ex: Her research appeared in a famous science journal.
The science journal asked other experts to check the paper.
He reads a science journal every month.
The training gave nurses different scenarios to practice.
We talked about scenarios for the trip if it rained.
The test used real-life scenarios at work.

wordDefs.def: A person or thing in a story
ex: The main character in the book is a young doctor.
My favorite character in the movie is the dog.
Each character in the play has a secret.

wordDefs.def: How a person is feeling at a certain time
ex: Her emotional state was better after a good night's sleep.
Music can change your emotional state quickly.
The nurse asked about his emotional state after the news.

wordDefs.def: Gave a score to show how good or strong something is
ex: Customers rated the hotel four out of five stars.
We rated each movie from one to ten.
She rated her pain as a seven.

wordDefs.def: Noticing or knowing what is happening
ex: Be aware of the cars when you cross the street.
I wasn't aware that the store had closed.
The driver was aware of the ice on the road.

wordDefs.def: The place and things around a person or thing
ex: The cat slowly got used to its new surroundings.
Hikers should pay attention to their surroundings.
She works best in quiet surroundings.

wordDefs.def: A big and easy-to-see difference between two things
ex: There is a clear gap between rich and poor families in the city.
The test showed a clear gap between the two classes.
We saw a clear gap in prices between the two stores.

wordDefs.def: Reacting quickly and well to what happens
ex: The new phone screen is very responsive.
Our landlord is responsive when something breaks.
Babies become more responsive to voices as they grow.

wordDefs.def: Formed an opinion about someone or something
ex: She judged the soup to be too salty.
People often judged him by his clothes.
The teacher judged our speeches on clear speaking.

wordDefs.def: A person who studies big questions about life, mind and truth
ex: The philosopher wrote a book about free will.
My professor is a philosopher who studies ethics.
Ancient Greek philosophers asked what makes a good life.

wordDefs.def: To not have enough of something
ex: Many towns lack enough doctors.
The plan lacks clear goals.
We lack the money for a new car.

wordDefs.def: One of the most important writers of a research paper, often the leader
ex: The senior author of the paper runs a lab in Boston.
Reporters asked the senior author about the results.
She was the senior author on three studies last year.

wordDefs.def: The sense inside you that tells you what is right and wrong
ex: His conscience told him to return the wallet.
She had a guilty conscience after the lie.
Let your conscience guide you.

wordDefs.def: The words a person decides to use
ex: Good word choice makes an essay easier to read.
The teacher praised my word choice in the poem.
His careless word choice upset some readers.

mainIdea.s: A study from Munich found that people rate AI as less conscious than humans, even when both act the same. When the question used the word aware, the difference mostly disappeared.
mainIdea.why: Even the most responsive AI fell behind the least responsive human on consciousness. With the word aware, the gap mostly went away.

mainIdea.s: Researchers say readers can easily spot whether a character in a short story is a person or a machine. Because AI behaves in an odd way, people give it lower scores for consciousness.
mainIdea.why: Close, but the AI and the human did exactly the same things. Nobody could tell them apart by their actions, yet people still rated the AI lower.

mainIdea.s: A university in Germany has built a new chatbot that its makers say can feel real emotions. They plan to test it with teachers and nurses before they start selling it next year.
mainIdea.why: This story is about a study of how people judge AI. Researchers looked into whether people think AI is conscious, not a new chatbot.

tf.s: Researchers looked into whether people think AI is conscious.
tf.why: A team in Munich studied this question and shared the results in a science journal.

tf.s: The most responsive AI was rated more conscious than any human.
tf.why: Even the most responsive AI fell behind the least responsive human on consciousness.

tf.s: In the stories, the AI and the human did exactly the same things.
tf.why: The two versions of each story were the same, so nobody could tell them apart by their actions.

tf.s: People judged awareness in AI and humans in very different ways.
tf.why: Awareness was judged in much the same way for both, and the gap mostly went away.

tf.s: The study shows that AI systems are truly conscious.
tf.why: The study does not try to figure out whether AI really is conscious. It looks at how people judge AI.

tf.s: A senior author said companies and journalists often talk up AI.
tf.why: He said they describe AI as having plans and even a conscience, so word choice matters.

lines.text: Did you see that study about AI and consciousness?
Researchers in Munich {{looked into}} whether people think AI is conscious.
Well, chatbots do {{come across as}} pretty human sometimes.
Sure. So the team {{set up}} short stories where an AI and a human did exactly the same things.
So you couldn't {{tell them apart}} by what they did?
Right. A character might react to a sound or {{pick up on}} someone's feelings.
And people still gave the AI lower scores?
Yes. Even the most responsive AI {{fell behind}} the least responsive human.
So people just won't call a machine conscious.
Exactly. But the word aware is [[a whole different story]]. With that word, the gap mostly {{went away}}.
Interesting. So the word itself [[makes all the difference]].
I think so. My [[gut feeling]] is that, [[deep down]], people still see AI as a tool.
Then why do companies {{talk up}} AI so much?
One of the researchers said that's why word choice matters.
Does the study say if AI is actually conscious?
No. It doesn't try to {{figure that out}}. That's still [[up for debate]].
Got it. I'll be more careful with the words I use for AI.

expressions.def: Used to say that one thing changes a result a lot
ex: A good night's sleep makes all the difference before a test.
Fresh bread makes all the difference in a sandwich.

expressions.def: Used to say that something is very different from what you just talked about
ex: Driving in the city is easy, but driving in the snow is a whole different story.

expressions.def: A strong idea you have without being able to explain why
ex: I had a gut feeling that the train would be late.
Trust your gut feeling about that job.

expressions.def: In your true feelings, even if you do not show them
ex: Deep down, he knew she was right.

expressions.def: Not decided yet, because people still disagree about it
ex: Whether the new school rule is fair is still up for debate.
The best age to buy a first phone is up for debate.
